title: The Complicated Future of Student Loans

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档关于对设计的热爱以及围绕设计的文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店里用黑胶唱片打碟的那个年代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着你最珍视的 300 件宝贝去工作，把 DJ 台变成了一个充满 50 年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼带来的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Natalie Kittroweff, in for Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的娜塔莉·基特罗夫，代班迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Last Friday, the Supreme Court struck down President Biden's sweeping plan to cancel billions of dollars in student loan debt.
sentences.zh: 上周五，最高法院驳回了拜登总统取消数十亿美元学生贷款债务的全面计划。

sentences.en: Today,
sentences.zh: 今天，

sentences.en: my colleague Stacey Cowley on what the court's decision means for borrowers now facing their first payments since the pandemic and how an alternative plan could still ease their burden.
sentences.zh: 我的同事斯泰西·考利将探讨最高法院的裁决对那些自疫情以来首次面临还款的借款人意味着什么，以及替代方案如何仍能减轻他们的负担。

sentences.en: It's Friday, July 7th.
sentences.zh: 今天是 7 月 7 日，星期五。

sentences.en: Stacey, welcome back.
sentences.zh: 斯泰西，欢迎回来。

sentences.en: And Natalie, welcome back.
sentences.zh: 娜塔莉，也欢迎你回来。

sentences.en: You're guest hosting again.
sentences.zh: 你又来做客座主持了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Imagine my surprise.
sentences.zh: 想象一下我的惊讶。

sentences.en: The last time I was guest hosting The Daily, there was big student loan news.
sentences.zh: 我上次客座主持《每日新闻》时，就有关于学生贷款的大新闻。

sentences.en: And now here I am back with you to talk about more student loan news.
sentences.zh: 现在我又回来和你讨论更多的学生贷款新闻了。

sentences.en: It's a wonky but fun duo act we have going.
sentences.zh: 我们这搭档组合虽然有点古怪，但还挺有趣的。

sentences.en: So last time, you and I spoke about President Biden's plan to forgive billions of dollars in student debt.
sentences.zh: 上次你我谈到了拜登总统免除数十亿美元学生债务的计划。

sentences.en: That was a plan that had generated a lot of controversy.
sentences.zh: 那是一个引发了巨大争议的计划。

sentences.en: And now, just last week, the Supreme Court struck it down.
sentences.zh: 而就在上周，最高法院驳回了它。

sentences.en: Remind me how that issue got to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 提醒我一下，这个问题是怎么闹到最高法院的？

sentences.en: What was Biden trying to do?
sentences.zh: 拜登当时想做什么？

sentences.en: So the problem the president was trying to tackle here was the issue of crippling student loan debt.
sentences.zh: 总统试图解决的问题是沉重的学生贷款债务。

sentences.en: Over the past roughly two decades, the cost of higher education has completely soared.
sentences.zh: 在过去大约二十年里，高等教育的成本完全飙升了。

sentences.en: Student debt loads have roughly tripled in the past 20 years.
sentences.zh: 过去 20 年里，学生债务负担大约增加了两倍。

sentences.en: For many people, their student loan bill is the biggest monthly bill in their lives now.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，学生贷款账单现在是他们生活中最大的月度账单。

sentences.en: More than 45 million people owe the federal government money for their student loans, and they owe a total of $1.6 trillion.
sentences.zh: 超过 4500 万人欠联邦政府学生贷款，总额达 1.6 万亿美元。

sentences.en: That eclipses all other consumer debts other than mortgages.
sentences.zh: 这超过了除抵押贷款以外的所有其他消费者债务。

sentences.en: For many people, it's bigger than their rent bill, bigger than their car payments, bigger than their credit cards, bigger than any other bill that they're paying.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，这比房租、车贷、信用卡账单，以及他们支付的任何其他账单都要多。

sentences.en: So back in March 2020, as a pandemic emergency measure,
sentences.zh: 回到 2020 年 3 月，作为一项疫情紧急措施，

sentences.en: President Donald Trump approved a timeout.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统批准了一个暂停期。

sentences.en: The idea was that people were under huge financial stress because of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 当时的想法是，人们因为疫情承受着巨大的经济压力。

sentences.en: Lots of people were losing their jobs.
sentences.zh: 很多人失去了工作。

sentences.en: And to give people more breathing room, they decided that this would be put on pause, that no one would have to pay their federal student loan bills for some period of time.
sentences.zh: 为了给人们更多的喘息空间，他们决定暂停还款，即在一段时间内，任何人都不必支付联邦学生贷款账单。

sentences.en: What ended up happening is those pauses just kept being extended over and over again.
sentences.zh: 结果就是这些暂停期被一次又一次地延长。

sentences.en: President Trump continued them throughout his entire administration.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统在他整个任期内都延续了这一政策。

sentences.en: As soon as President Biden took office on his very first day in office, he extended the pause, and that just kept going and going and going.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统上任的第一天就延长了暂停期，之后就一直延续下去。

sentences.en: Meaning anyone who owed the government money for their education didn't have to make a single payment on that debt during the pause.
sentences.zh: 这意味着任何欠政府教育贷款的人在暂停期间都不必偿还一分钱。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And for many people, this was an enormous change.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，这是一个巨大的改变。

sentences.en: I mean, certainly for people who lost their jobs, this was a very helpful temporary measure to tide them over.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对于那些失业的人来说，这无疑是一个非常有帮助的临时措施，帮他们度过了难关。

sentences.en: But also for people who did keep their jobs, this just changed their household finances completely.
sentences.zh: 但对于那些保住工作的人来说，这也彻底改变了他们的家庭财务状况。

sentences.en: I was speaking recently with one borrower.
sentences.zh: 我最近和一位借款人谈过。

sentences.en: His name is Victor.
sentences.zh: 他叫维克多。

sentences.en: He lives right outside the Denver area.
sentences.zh: 他住在丹佛郊区。

sentences.en: And he and his wife had been paying over $1,000 a month for their student loans.
sentences.zh: 他和妻子以前每月要支付超过 1000 美元的学生贷款。

sentences.en: Once that went away, they looked at each other and said, we can afford to use that money to buy a house.
sentences.zh: 一旦这笔支出消失了，他们看着对方说，我们可以用这笔钱买房了。

sentences.en: So in June 2020, they were able to buy their first home together.
sentences.zh: 所以 2020 年 6 月，他们成功买下了他们的第一套房。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: But this timeout was always intended to be temporary.
sentences.zh: 但这个暂停期本意是暂时的。

sentences.en: And the law Biden was using to do it in particular relied upon the education secretary being able to do this in a time of national emergency.
sentences.zh: 而且拜登用来实施该政策的法律，特别依赖于教育部长在国家紧急状态下采取行动的能力。

sentences.en: It's pretty hard to make the case that the coronavirus is still a national emergency.
sentences.zh: 要说新冠疫情现在仍然是国家紧急状态，这很难站得住脚。

sentences.en: So this was going to have to, as much as this temporary extension went on and on, as long as it did, it was going to at some point have to end.
sentences.zh: 所以，无论这个临时延期持续了多久，它最终都必须结束。

sentences.en: And part of the problem the administration was facing, why they didn't want to just pick back up exactly where we were before the pandemic,
sentences.zh: 政府面临的部分问题，以及为什么他们不想直接回到疫情前的状态，

sentences.en: is this is a system that had been pretty badly broken for years.
sentences.zh: 是因为这个系统多年来已经相当糟糕了。

sentences.en: Lots of people had been falling into default.
sentences.zh: 很多人已经陷入违约。

sentences.en: A lot of people had been struggling with bills they could not afford to pay before the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 疫情前，很多人就已经在为无法负担的账单而挣扎。

sentences.en: So the solution the Biden administration came to was to say, if we're going to restart this, let's try to really fix it.
sentences.zh: 所以拜登政府想出的解决方案是：如果我们打算重启，那就试着彻底解决它。

sentences.en: Let's do something big and dramatic.
sentences.zh: 让我们做一些重大而戏剧性的事情。

sentences.en: My campaign for president, I made a commitment.
sentences.zh: 我在竞选总统时做出了承诺。

sentences.en: I made a commitment that would provide student debt relief.
sentences.zh: 我承诺将提供学生债务减免。

sentences.en: And I'm honoring that commitment today.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在兑现这一承诺。

sentences.en: And that big dramatic thing was the debt cancellation plan we discussed last summer.
sentences.zh: 而那个重大且戏剧性的举措就是我们去年夏天讨论的债务取消计划。

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: With today's announcement, the government is forgiving $10,000 in federal loans for anyone earning less than $125,000 a year.
sentences.zh: 随着今天的宣布，政府将为年收入低于 12.5 万美元的任何人免除 1 万美元的联邦贷款。

sentences.en: And canceling up to $20,000 in student loans for those who received Pell Grants.
sentences.zh: 并为那些获得佩尔助学金的人取消最高 2 万美元的学生贷款。

sentences.en: This is something that progressive activists in particular had been pushing for for many years.
sentences.zh: 这正是进步派活动人士多年来一直推动的事情。

sentences.en: This idea that pretty much everyone who had a federal student loan debt would get some chunk of it written off and forgiven.
sentences.zh: 即几乎所有背负联邦学生贷款债务的人都能免除其中的一部分。

sentences.en: People can start, finally crawl out from under that mountain of debt.
sentences.zh: 人们终于可以开始从那座债务大山下爬出来了。

sentences.en: To get on top of their rent and their utilities.
sentences.zh: 去支付房租和水电费。

sentences.en: To finally think about buying a home or starting a family or starting a business.
sentences.zh: 终于可以考虑买房、组建家庭或创业了。

sentences.en: So what this plan did collectively was it targeted a lot of the relief to low-income families and to non-white borrowers.
sentences.zh: 所以这个计划总的来说，是将大部分减免针对低收入家庭和非白人借款人。

sentences.en: So for borrowers of color in particular, this was going to be a pretty major financial windfall.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于有色人种借款人来说，这无疑是一笔重大的经济意外之财。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I remember this was going to cost a lot of money, right?
sentences.zh: 我记得这要花很多钱，对吧？

sentences.en: But it could potentially help a ton of people.
sentences.zh: 但它可能帮助很多人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The price tag on this was over $400 billion.
sentences.zh: 这笔开支超过了 4000 亿美元。

sentences.en: So it would have been one of the most expensive executive actions in American history.
sentences.zh: 所以它本将成为美国历史上最昂贵的行政行动之一。

sentences.en: But it would also have helped quite a few people.
sentences.zh: 但它也会帮助相当多的人。

sentences.en: The estimate was that up to 40 million people were going to be eligible for some level of debt cancellation.
sentences.zh: 据估计，多达 4000 万人有资格获得一定程度的债务减免。

sentences.en: And that around 20 million would have seen their entire student loan balance wiped out.
sentences.zh: 大约 2000 万人的全部学生贷款余额将被清零。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: But there was also a real problem with this in that it quickly became a political lightning rod.
sentences.zh: 但这也存在一个真正的问题，因为它很快就成了政治避雷针。

sentences.en: No one's paying off Arkansas Farmers tractor loans.
sentences.zh: 没人帮阿肯色州的农民还拖拉机贷款。

sentences.en: No one's paying off their small business loans.
sentences.zh: 没人帮他们还小企业贷款。

sentences.en: No one's paying off their mortgage.
sentences.zh: 没人帮他们还抵押贷款。

sentences.en: Republicans had some real political pushback around the idea of why should people who have paid off their loans subsidize those who haven't?
sentences.zh: 共和党人对“为什么已经还清贷款的人要补贴那些还没还清的人”这一想法提出了真正的政治反弹。

sentences.en: Is this just a big giveaway to this educated class of borrowers?
sentences.zh: 这难道不是给受过教育的借款阶层的一份大礼吗？

sentences.en: Senator Mitch McConnell calling it a slap in the face to every family who sacrificed to save for college, every graduate who paid their debt.
sentences.zh: 参议员米奇·麦康奈尔称其为“对每个为上大学而牺牲储蓄的家庭，以及每个偿还了债务的毕业生的打脸”。

sentences.en: And also it became a big legal issue in that this was a $400 billion program.
sentences.zh: 而且这也成了一个重大的法律问题，因为这是一个 4000 亿美元的项目。

sentences.en: And Biden was really swinging on this one in terms of the legal standing to do it.
sentences.zh: 拜登在法律依据方面确实是在孤注一掷。

sentences.en: So that's where the court challenges arose.
sentences.zh: 所以法律挑战随之而来。

sentences.en: A group of Republican-led states came together and sued to stop this.
sentences.zh: 一群由共和党领导的州联合起来起诉以阻止这一计划。

sentences.en: And what was the argument behind that lawsuit?
sentences.zh: 那场诉讼背后的论点是什么？

sentences.en: The core challenge to what Biden had done legally was that the law that Biden had used to do this, an act called the HEROES Act, didn't give him this power.
sentences.zh: 对拜登法律行为的核心挑战在于，拜登用来实施该计划的法律——即《英雄法案》——并没有赋予他这种权力。

sentences.en: That law gave the Secretary of Education the ability to waive or modify student loan debt.
sentences.zh: 该法律赋予教育部长豁免或修改学生贷款债务的能力。

sentences.en: The argument the states made was that doesn't translate to the ability to unilaterally wipe out billions and billions of dollars worth of student loan debt.
sentences.zh: 各州提出的论点是，这并不意味着有权单方面抹去数十亿美元的学生贷款债务。

sentences.en: The suit's saying that Biden needed to consult Congress to do something this big.
sentences.zh: 诉讼称，拜登在做如此重大的事情时需要咨询国会。

sentences.en: The suit was directly saying that, that Congress controls the power of the purse, that if you're going to cancel hundreds of billions of dollars in student loans,
sentences.zh: 诉讼直接指出，国会掌握着钱袋子权力，如果你要取消数千亿美元的学生贷款，

sentences.en: that needs to be a decision Congress clearly makes, that the president does not have the sole authority to do it.
sentences.zh: 那必须是国会明确做出的决定，总统没有单独的权力来做这件事。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So as this lawsuit made its way through the court system,
sentences.zh: 随着诉讼在法院系统中推进，

sentences.en: Biden was forced to put the entire student debt forgiveness program on hold.
sentences.zh: 拜登被迫将整个学生债务减免计划搁置。

sentences.en: Literally at the last second, as they're right about to start canceling debt for tens of millions of people who've applied for this program, they hit pause, freeze the program,
sentences.zh: 就在最后一刻，当他们即将为数千万申请该计划的人取消债务时，他们按下了暂停键，冻结了该计划，

sentences.en: and wait for the court challenges to work their way through up to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 并等待法律挑战一路打到最高法院。

sentences.en: And so last Friday, we get a decision from the court.
sentences.zh: 所以上周五，我们收到了法院的裁决。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the court sides with the states in this case.
sentences.zh: 法院在本案中站在了各州一边。

sentences.en: The court majority says pretty clearly that they agree that the president does not have the power under this law to do this, and that if this level of debt cancellation is going
sentences.zh: 法院多数派非常明确地表示，他们同意总统在该法律下没有权力这样做，如果这种程度的债务取消要发生，

sentences.en: to occur, it has to be a decision made by Congress.
sentences.zh: 它必须是国会做出的决定。

sentences.en: So basically, this is the Supreme Court saying that for now, mass student debt cancellation is off the table.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，这是最高法院在说，目前大规模学生债务取消是不可能的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And also, this was the Supreme Court saying this pretty definitively, that this is not something this president or any president is going to be able to do unilaterally.
sentences.zh: 而且最高法院也非常明确地表示，这不是这位总统或任何总统能够单方面做到的事情。

sentences.en: I think this decision did very firmly kick this issue back to Congress and make it clear
sentences.zh: 我认为这一裁决非常坚定地将这个问题踢回给了国会，并明确表示

sentences.en: that if anything of this scale is going to happen, it's going to have to be done by Congress.
sentences.zh: 如果这种规模的事情要发生，必须由国会来完成。

sentences.en: And the reason that hasn't happened is that Congress simply hasn't had the votes to do it.
sentences.zh: 而之所以没有发生，是因为国会根本没有足够的票数来通过它。

sentences.en: Even when Democrats controlled both chambers, the Senate didn't have the votes to pass it.
sentences.zh: 即使在民主党控制两院时，参议院也没有足够的票数通过。

sentences.en: And certainly now that the Republicans control the House, there's really no prospect in the near future of Congress taking this up.
sentences.zh: 当然，现在共和党控制了众议院，国会在不久的将来处理此事的可能性确实很小。

sentences.en: So what was the reaction to the decision?
sentences.zh: 那么对这一裁决的反应是什么？

sentences.en: It was not entirely shocked, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 老实说，并不完全令人震惊。

sentences.en: This is a conservative court, and people were kind of braced for this decision.
sentences.zh: 这是一个保守派法院，人们已经为这个裁决做好了心理准备。

sentences.en: But certainly, it was a gut punch for a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 但可以肯定的是，这对很多人来说是一个沉重的打击。

sentences.en: There are people who were really relying on this to get rid of a debt that had haunted them, in some cases, for decades.
sentences.zh: 有些人真的指望用这个来摆脱困扰他们几十年的债务。

sentences.en: And this is especially coming at a fraught time for people, because in October, these payments resume.
sentences.zh: 而且这正值人们处于焦虑时刻，因为十月份还款就要恢复了。

sentences.en: So people are being told, not only are you not going to get this cancellation, but in just a couple of months, you're going to have to start sending in checks again.
sentences.zh: 所以人们被告知，不仅你不会得到减免，而且在短短几个月内，你还得开始重新寄出支票。

sentences.en: So this moment feels like a pretty big setback for Biden.
sentences.zh: 所以这一刻对拜登来说感觉是一个相当大的挫折。

sentences.en: I mean, eliminating student debt was one of his big campaign promises, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，消除学生债务是他竞选时的重大承诺之一，对吧？

sentences.en: And it's hugely popular with his base, especially younger people.
sentences.zh: 而且这在他的选民基础中非常受欢迎，尤其是年轻人。

sentences.en: The Supreme Court blocks it right before people are going to have to start repaying the debt.
sentences.zh: 最高法院在人们必须开始偿还债务之前就阻止了它。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, this was a huge blow for Biden.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这对拜登来说是一个巨大的打击。

sentences.en: This had become one of his signature efforts.
sentences.zh: 这已经成为他标志性的努力之一。

sentences.en: This was something that was really important to tens of millions of people.
sentences.zh: 这对数千万人来说确实非常重要。

sentences.en: Let me begin by saying I know there are millions of Americans, millions of Americans in this
sentences.zh: 首先我想说，我知道在这个国家有数百万美国人，数百万美国人

sentences.en: country who feel disappointed and discouraged or even a little bit angry about the court's decision today on student debt.
sentences.zh: 对法院今天关于学生债务的裁决感到失望、沮丧，甚至有点愤怒。

sentences.en: So Biden gives a press conference at the White House on Friday attacking this decision.
sentences.zh: 所以拜登周五在白宫举行新闻发布会，抨击了这一裁决。

sentences.en: Republican elected officials and special interests stepped in.
sentences.zh: 共和党民选官员和特殊利益集团介入了。

sentences.en: They said, no, no.
sentences.zh: 他们说，不，不。

sentences.en: And really firmly pointed the finger back at the Supreme Court and the Republicans.
sentences.zh: 他非常坚定地将矛头指向了最高法院和共和党人。

sentences.en: You know, these Republican officials just couldn't bear the thought of providing relief for working class, middle class Americans.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些共和党官员只是无法忍受为工薪阶层、中产阶级美国人提供救济的想法。

sentences.en: He said over and over that this was the Republican Party choosing to try to block this.
sentences.zh: 他反复说这是共和党选择试图阻止这一计划。

sentences.en: I believe the court's decision to strike down my student debt relief program as a mistake was wrong.
sentences.zh: 我相信法院驳回我的学生债务减免计划的决定是一个错误，是错误的。

sentences.en: And that this was the Supreme Court doing what he thought was a misinterpretation of the law.
sentences.zh: 而且这是最高法院在做他认为是对法律的误读。

sentences.en: But wasn't it always kind of a moonshot to try to cancel federal student loan debt?
sentences.zh: 但试图取消联邦学生贷款债务难道不是一直有点像天方夜谭吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I'm sure for people who have a bunch of debt, it sounds great, but it also just seems like it might have been unlikely from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我相信对于背负大量债务的人来说，这听起来很棒，但从一开始似乎就不太可能实现。

sentences.en: Yes, this was always, as you said, a moonshot and kind of a gamble.
sentences.zh: 是的，正如你所说，这一直是一个天方夜谭，也是一种赌博。

sentences.en: And there was always the chance that it was going to get blocked.
sentences.zh: 而且它一直有被阻止的风险。

sentences.en: We need to find a new way.
sentences.zh: 我们需要找到一条新路。

sentences.en: And we're moving as fast as we can.
sentences.zh: 我们正在尽全力推进。

sentences.en: But the reality is that while this was pretty important, it was only one piece of a larger plan for overhauling the student loan system.
sentences.zh: 但现实情况是，虽然这很重要，但这只是彻底改革学生贷款体系这一宏大计划中的一环。

sentences.en: Today's decision has closed one path.
sentences.zh: 今天的裁决堵死了一条路。

sentences.en: Now we're going to pursue another.
sentences.zh: 现在我们要寻求另一条路。

sentences.en: And the other elements of that plan are still going ahead.
sentences.zh: 而该计划的其他部分仍将继续推进。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我凌晨四点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空探索七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最强的队伍。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝成立175周年，致力于帮助您了解世界，充实每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享特别优惠，请访问 nytimes.com/subscribe。

sentences.en: Stacey, before the break, you said there were these other elements of debt relief that were on the way.
sentences.zh: 斯泰西，休息前你提到还有其他债务减免措施即将推出。

sentences.en: What are those?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: So debt cancellation was the biggest and flashiest and simplest piece of President Biden's plan.
sentences.zh: 债务取消是拜登总统计划中规模最大、最引人注目也最简单的一环。

sentences.en: But there's a whole bunch of other elements of this plan that are still prepared to move forward that the Supreme Court hasn't touched.
sentences.zh: 但该计划中还有许多其他部分准备推进，且最高法院并未触及这些部分。

sentences.en: And again, the biggest one there is going to affect for millions of people how much they actually pay on their loans.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，其中最重要的一项将影响数百万人的实际贷款还款额。

sentences.en: What Biden has been planning since late last year is a new payment plan for those who are on income driven payments.
sentences.zh: 拜登从去年年底开始筹划的是一项针对收入驱动型还款人群的新还款计划。

sentences.en: What's that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: So there's several different ways you can pay your student loan bill.
sentences.zh: 偿还学生贷款有几种不同的方式。

sentences.en: The default plan is that you just pay it in chunks over the course of 10 years.
sentences.zh: 默认方案是你在10年内分期还清。

sentences.en: And if you can make that number, great.
sentences.zh: 如果你能负担这个数额，那很好。

sentences.en: But a lot of people can't afford that number.
sentences.zh: 但很多人负担不起。

sentences.en: So the government instead offers what's called income based repayment plans, where the amount you owe each month is directly tied to your income.
sentences.zh: 所以政府提供了所谓的“收入驱动型还款计划”，你每月的还款额直接与你的收入挂钩。

sentences.en: Meaning monthly payments are a function of a borrower's income.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，月供是借款人收入的函数。

sentences.en: If you make less, you owe less.
sentences.zh: 收入越少，还款越少。

sentences.en: If you make more, you owe more every month.
sentences.zh: 收入越多，每月还款越多。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And what the Biden administration has done here is designed a completely new income driven plan that's very different than the ones we've seen before.
sentences.zh: 拜登政府在这里所做的是设计了一套全新的收入驱动型计划，与我们之前看到的截然不同。

sentences.en: How so?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: The biggest pieces of this is there's two really dramatic things.
sentences.zh: 其中最重大的部分包含两项非常显著的改变。

sentences.en: The first is that it would cap the amount that you owe for undergraduate loans at no more than 5% of your income.
sentences.zh: 首先，它将本科贷款的还款额上限设定为不超过你收入的5%。

sentences.en: What your income is, is calculated through a slightly complicated formula that exempts a certain amount below the poverty line.
sentences.zh: 你的收入是通过一个稍微复杂的公式计算出来的，该公式会豁免贫困线以下的一定金额。

sentences.en: But basically, they're looking at what's called your discretionary income.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，他们看的是所谓的“可支配收入”。

sentences.en: And under the existing payment plans, you owe up to 10% of that amount to pay off your loans.
sentences.zh: 在现有的还款计划下，你需要拿出该金额的10%来偿还贷款。

sentences.en: This cuts it to 5%.
sentences.zh: 这将其削减到了5%。

sentences.en: That right there means that millions of people are going to see their monthly student loan bill cut in half.
sentences.zh: 这意味着数百万人的每月学生贷款账单将直接减半。

sentences.en: That seems pretty significant.
sentences.zh: 这看起来相当重要。

sentences.en: Yes, it definitely is, especially when paired with the second change that's in this new program, which is that interest will not accrue for people who are making their monthly
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此，尤其是当它与该新计划中的第二项改革相结合时，即对于按月还款的人来说，利息将不再累积。

sentences.en: payments.
sentences.zh: 还款。

sentences.en: That is an enormous change in how student loans operate.
sentences.zh: 这是学生贷款运作方式上的巨大变革。

sentences.en: What's been really frustrating for many people over the years is that these interest payments can often eclipse what you're paying on your monthly bill.
sentences.zh: 多年来让许多人感到沮丧的是，这些利息支出往往会超过你每月账单的还款额。

sentences.en: Every penny you send in is being used to pay down interest and your debt actually isn't decreasing.
sentences.zh: 你汇出的每一分钱都被用来支付利息，而你的债务实际上并没有减少。

sentences.en: I talked to a gentleman named Claude Reed, who took out $3,300 in loans back in the early
sentences.zh: 我采访了一位名叫克劳德·里德的先生，他在70年代初申请了3,300美元的贷款。
70年代。

sentences.en: He's been making payments since then.
sentences.zh: 从那时起他一直在还款。

sentences.en: He's paid over $9,000 on his loans over the years.
sentences.zh: 多年来他已经为贷款支付了超过9,000美元。

sentences.en: But with interest in fees, the balance keeps going up.
sentences.zh: 但加上利息和费用，余额却一直在增加。

sentences.en: So right now, he still owes $4,600, more than he borrowed originally.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，他仍然欠款4,600美元，比他最初借的还要多。

sentences.en: And for many borrowers, that's an incredibly frustrating and common experience to feel like
sentences.zh: 对于许多借款人来说，这是一种极其令人沮丧且普遍的经历，感觉

sentences.en: they're throwing this money at payments every month and the number on their bill just keeps rising.
sentences.zh: 他们每个月都在还钱，但账单上的数字却不断上涨。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And what this plan says is for the first time, if you are sending in your payment each month, that money is going to go straight towards decreasing your balance.
sentences.zh: 而这项计划规定，从现在起，如果你每月按时还款，这笔钱将直接用于减少你的余额。

sentences.en: That's going to be a huge psychological change for people because one of the biggest barriers
sentences.zh: 这对人们来说将是一个巨大的心理转变，因为学生贷款最大的障碍之一

sentences.en: with student loans is this sense of I'm throwing money at this every month and it keeps going up.
sentences.zh: 就是这种感觉：我每个月都在还钱，但欠款却在不断增加。

sentences.en: I'm not making any progress.
sentences.zh: 我没有任何进展。

sentences.en: This will change that.
sentences.zh: 这将改变现状。

sentences.en: Okay, so now for people like Claude Reed, what you're saying is that the amount they owe every month is not going to get bigger as long as they stay current on their payments.
sentences.zh: 好的，那么对于像克劳德·里德这样的人，你的意思是，只要他们保持按时还款，他们每月的欠款额就不会再增加了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And there's one more thing here, which is that it's always been possible to qualify for a $0 monthly payment.
sentences.zh: 还有一点，那就是一直以来都有可能获得“0美元月供”的资格。

sentences.en: If your income is very low, you can qualify to not have to make a monthly payment.
sentences.zh: 如果你的收入非常低，你就有资格无需每月还款。

sentences.en: This new plan tinkers with the formula there a bit and expands the group of people who are going to qualify for that.
sentences.zh: 这项新计划对其中的公式做了一些微调，并扩大了符合该资格的人群范围。

sentences.en: But that's going to have a big impact for people on the lowest end of the income spectrum.
sentences.zh: 但这将对收入处于最低端的人群产生重大影响。

sentences.en: Certainly anyone making minimum wage is going to qualify for this $0 monthly payment.
sentences.zh: 当然，任何拿最低工资的人都有资格获得这0美元的月供。

sentences.en: And this is intended both to help those borrowers and also to help the government a bit.
sentences.zh: 这旨在既帮助这些借款人，也对政府有所帮助。

sentences.en: It wants these people to stop falling into default.
sentences.zh: 它希望这些人不再陷入违约。

sentences.en: It wants these people to have an easier pathway to remain current on their loans.
sentences.zh: 它希望这些人能有一条更轻松的途径来保持贷款状态正常。

sentences.en: So by expanding the group of people who are going to qualify for no payment because they just don't have the income to really make any payments, that's intended to really be
sentences.zh: 因此，通过扩大那些因收入不足而无需还款的人群范围，这旨在真正成为

sentences.en: a benefit for a growing number of people.
sentences.zh: 越来越多人的福利。

sentences.en: So just to recap, under the new plan, for many borrowers, their monthly payments will be cut in half.
sentences.zh: 所以总结一下，在新计划下，对于许多借款人来说，他们的月供将减半。

sentences.en: We're also going to see that overall debts won't get bigger with ballooning interests.
sentences.zh: 我们还将看到，总债务不会因为利息膨胀而增加。

sentences.en: And then for more borrowers who are in a really tough situation, maybe they've lost their job
sentences.zh: 对于那些处境非常艰难的借款人，也许他们失业了，

sentences.en: or they don't earn all that much money to start with, they will not have to make monthly payments at all.
sentences.zh: 或者他们本来就挣不了多少钱，他们将完全不必支付月供。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Cumulatively, that's going to be a really big set of changes for the student loan system.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，这对学生贷款体系来说将是一系列重大的变革。

sentences.en: And this is all coming and being done quite deliberately at a fairly critical time for the system because October is when payments restart.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是经过深思熟虑，在体系的关键时刻完成的，因为10月是恢复还款的时间。

sentences.en: So for borrowers who for more than three years now have not had to be making their payments, they're now going to have to start doing that again.
sentences.zh: 所以对于那些已经三年多没有还款的借款人来说，他们现在必须重新开始还款了。

sentences.en: And this is all intended to be kind of a reset to make that transition easier.
sentences.zh: 这一切旨在进行一种重置，使这种过渡更容易。

sentences.en: There's a few other things happening there as well.
sentences.zh: 还有一些其他事情也在发生。

sentences.en: One of the big ones is that the administration said last week that for the first 12 months, borrowers who are late on their payments or fall behind on them and don't make them
sentences.zh: 其中重要的一点是，政府上周表示，在最初的12个月内，那些还款逾期或落后而未还款的借款人

sentences.en: won't be reported to credit bureaus.
sentences.zh: 将不会被上报给征信机构。

sentences.en: So they're trying to kind of cushion the transition and soften the blow and give people time to get back to this idea of having this bill be part of their lives again.
sentences.zh: 所以他们试图缓冲这种过渡，减轻冲击，并给人们时间重新适应将这笔账单作为生活一部分的状态。

sentences.en: And Stacey, given what happened to Biden's last big attempt to rein in student debt, the
sentences.zh: 斯泰西，考虑到拜登上次试图控制学生债务的大动作，也就是

sentences.en: last big, sweepy effort, how do we know that this part of the plan is actually going to happen?
sentences.zh: 那次大规模的全面努力，我们怎么知道计划的这一部分真的会实现呢？

sentences.en: It's an excellent question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极好的问题。

sentences.en: On this one, the administration has said that they thought their authority to do this was crystal clear and that they would be surprised if there was legal challenges.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，政府表示他们认为自己这样做的权力非常明确，如果出现法律挑战，他们会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: And it is true that the law does give the education secretary the authority to design these repayment plans.
sentences.zh: 法律确实赋予了教育部长设计这些还款计划的权力，这一点是事实。

sentences.en: The education secretary has been doing that for decades.
sentences.zh: 教育部长几十年来一直都在这样做。

sentences.en: And this does seem to be on firmer ground as something that is a typical act that the education department can go forth and do.
sentences.zh: 这似乎确实有更坚实的基础，是教育部可以继续执行的典型行为。

sentences.en: Stacey, as you're describing all these changes, it strikes me that they're a pretty big deal, right?
sentences.zh: 斯泰西，当你描述所有这些变化时，我感觉它们意义重大，对吧？

sentences.en: But they don't have the emotional power of what we thought was going to happen, of getting rid of $20,000 of debt for a borrower overnight.
sentences.zh: 但它们没有我们原以为会发生的那种情感冲击力，即一夜之间为借款人免除2万美元债务。

sentences.en: And I guess I just, I wonder if these changes, as impactful as they may be, will feel transformative to people on an individual level.
sentences.zh: 我只是在想，这些变化尽管影响深远，但在个人层面上是否会让人感到具有变革性。

sentences.en: Yes, I think that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: The emotional element of this is going to be really challenging.
sentences.zh: 其中的情感因素将是非常具有挑战性的。

sentences.en: The reality is that this will be a very different student loan system than it was before the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 现实情况是，这将是一个与疫情前截然不同的学生贷款体系。

sentences.en: People's monthly bills are going to look very different.
sentences.zh: 人们的月度账单看起来会大不相同。

sentences.en: In many cases, they're going to be smaller, but we're also still going back to a world where
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，它们会变少，但我们仍然要回到这样一个世界：

sentences.en: after three years of having a $0 student loan payment, people are going to have to start once again paying hundreds or thousands of dollars a month on these debts.
sentences.zh: 在经历了三年0美元学生贷款还款后，人们将不得不再次开始每月支付数百或数千美元的债务。

sentences.en: And there's no way for that to happen without it feeling pretty unpleasant for people.
sentences.zh: 如果不让人感到非常不快，这是不可能实现的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And one of the upshots of the way this all played out was that people feel like something got snatched away.
sentences.zh: 这一切发展的结果之一是，人们感觉有什么东西被夺走了。

sentences.en: You know, people were promised this big debt relief, which would have been a big, exciting, very easy to understand thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们被承诺了这种大规模的债务减免，那本将是一件重大、令人兴奋且非常容易理解的事情。

sentences.en: And instead, that's gone.
sentences.zh: 而现在，那已经消失了。

sentences.en: And now we're left with going back into a more efficient, more affordable, but still, ultimately, it's a debt collection system.
sentences.zh: 我们现在剩下的是回归到一个更高效、更可负担，但归根结底仍然是一个债务催收的体系。

sentences.en: So even though the world in October, as we reenter these debt payments, is going to be better for a lot of people, it's still not necessarily going to feel better.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使10月当我们重新进入这些债务还款时，世界对许多人来说会变得更好，但它未必会让人感觉更好。

sentences.en: For a lot of people, there's just going to be this heavy sense of, I once again have to pick up and start paying this big, crushing debt.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，只会有一种沉重的感觉：我不得不再次拿起并开始偿还这笔沉重的债务。

sentences.en: Stacey, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 斯泰西，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks, Natalie.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，娜塔莉。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由人制作的，就像你刚才听到的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: On Thursday, Janet Yellen began a four-day trip to China, her first to the country as
sentences.zh: 周四，珍妮特·耶伦开始了为期四天的中国之行，这是她作为

sentences.en: Treasury Secretary.
sentences.zh: 财政部长首次访问中国。

sentences.en: The visit will be a challenging act of economic diplomacy, as Yellen attempts to ease years of distrust between the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这次访问将是一场充满挑战的经济外交行动，因为耶伦试图缓解美中之间多年来的不信任。

sentences.en: and China.
sentences.zh: 中国。

sentences.en: Both countries have continued to erect new barriers to trade and investment, particularly after the U.S.
sentences.zh: 两国都在继续设置新的贸易和投资壁垒，特别是在美国

sentences.en: began blocking China's access to sensitive technology, such as semiconductors, last year.
sentences.zh: 去年开始阻止中国获取半导体等敏感技术之后。

sentences.en: And for the first time in two decades, the federal government gave an Alzheimer's drug full approval.
sentences.zh: 这是二十年来联邦政府首次给予阿尔茨海默病药物全面批准。

sentences.en: The drug, Lakembi, has been shown to modestly slow cognitive decline in the early stages of the disease.
sentences.zh: 该药物名为Leqembi，已被证明可以适度减缓疾病早期的认知衰退。

sentences.en: And Medicare, the federal health insurance program for older Americans, said it would cover much of its high cost, laying the foundation for the drug's widespread use.
sentences.zh: 而为美国老年人提供联邦医疗保险的Medicare表示，它将覆盖该药大部分高昂的费用，为该药的广泛使用奠定了基础。

sentences.en: Data from a large clinical trial showed that the drug may slow decline by about five months
sentences.zh: 一项大型临床试验的数据显示，该药物可能在18个月内使轻度症状患者的衰退减缓约五个月，

sentences.en: over an 18-month period for people with mild symptoms, but that it also carries significant safety risks.
sentences.zh: 但它也带来了重大的安全风险。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一批自诩为改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就陷入了一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《地铁》节目中，我是主持人莎拉·凯尼格，为您讲述那些试图维持影响力却在过程中逐渐失控的人们的故事。
